la:noun:ludus.html:
lūdus, i, m.
id.
,
a play.
Lit.
In gen., a play, game, diversion, pastime: ad pilam se aut ad talos, aut ad tessaras conferunt, aut etiam novum sibi aliquem excogitant in otio ludum,: datur concessu omnium huic aliqui ludus aetati,: campestris,: nec lusisse pudet, sed non incidere ludum,.—
In partic.
Ludi, public games, plays, spectacles, shows, exhibitions, which were given in honor of the gods, etc.
In gen.: hoc praetore ludos Apollini faciente,: ludos committere,: ludos magnificentissimos apparare,: ludos apparatissimos magnificentissimosque facere,: ludos aspicere,: ludos persolvere alicui deo,: ludis, during the games, ap. ; : circus maximus ne diebus quidem ludorum Circensium ... irrigabatur,.—Sing.: haec ultra quid erit, nisi ludus?.—
In this sense, ludi is freq. in appos. with the neutr. plur. of the adj. which names the games: ludi Consualia,: ludi Cerealia,: ludi Taurilia, (Weissenb. Taurii); 34, 54, 3; cf.: quaedam faciem soloecismi habent ... ut tragoedia Thyestes, ut ludi Floralia ac Megalensia ... numquam aliter a veteribus dicta,; cf.: ludis Megalensibus,.—
Also with gen. of place: eo ipso die auditam esse eam pugnam ludis Olympiae memoriae proditum est,.—
Stage-plays (opp. to the games of the circus): venationes autem ludosque et cum collegā et separatim edidit,.—
A place of exercise or practice, a school for elementary instruction and discipline (cf. schola): in ludum ire,: fidicinus,music-school,: litterarius,: litterarum ludi,; : ludus discendi,: Dionysius Corinthi dicitur ludum aperuisse,: Isocrates, cujus e ludo, tamquam ex equo Trojano, meri principes exierunt,; : gladiatores, quos ibi Caesar in ludo habebat,: militaris,: litterarii paene ista sunt ludi et trivialis scientiae,: litterarium ludum exercere,: obsides quosdam abductos e litterario ludo,: ibi namque (in foro) in tabernis litterarum ludi erant,: quem puerum in ludo cognōrat,: in Flavī ludum me mittere,; cf. ; ; : sic veniunt ad miscellanea ludi,.
Transf.
Play, sport, i. e. any thing done, as it were, in play, without trouble, mere sport, child's play: oratio ludus est homini non hebeti,: cum illa perdiscere ludus esset,: quibus (Graecis) jusjurandum jocus est, testimonium ludus,.—
Sport, jest, joke, fun: si vis videre ludos

jucundissimos, : ad honores per ludum et per neglegentiam pervenire,: aliquem per ludum et jocum evertere,, § 155: amoto quaeramus seria ludo,: vertere seria ludo,: nil per ludum simulabitur,: ut ludos facit,: ludos facere aliquem, to make sport of, make game of, to banter, jeer at, mock: ut nunc is te ludos facit,: quem, senecta aetate, ludos facias,.— With dat.: miris modis dī ludos faciunt hominibus,; .—In pass.: ludos fieri,: hocine me aetatis ludos vis factum esse indigne?: ludos aliquem dimittere, to send one away with scorn and derision, or, as in Engl., to send one off with a flea in his ear: numquam hercle quisquam me lenonem dixerit, si te non ludos pessimos dimisero,: ludos facis me,: facere ludos aliquid, to make a jest or a trifle of any thing, to throw away, to lose: nunc et operam ludos facit, et retia, etc.,: ludos dare, praebere,to make one's self ridiculous,: ludos alicui reddere,to play tricks on,: dare ludum alicui, to give play to one, i. e. to humor, indulge, ; ; : amori dare ludum,: ludus aetatis, the pleasures of love: si frui liceret ludo aetatis, praesertim recto et legitimo amore,.—

Ludus, the title of a work of Nævius: ut est in Naevii Ludo,; Fest. s. v. redhostire, p. 270, 22 Müll.—Also, Ludus de Morte Claudii, a work of Seneca.

senses: to deceive, delude, trick, take advantage of
la:verb:ludo.html:
lūdo, si, sum (
inf. ludier, ), 3, v. a. and n.
root lud- for loid-, from Sanscr. krīd, to play; cf. laus and cluere from Sanscr. root cru-
, to play.
Lit., to play, play at a game of some kind: tesseris,: aleā ludere,: pilā et duodecim scriptis,; ; : cum pila,: trocho,: nucibus,: pilā,: positā luditur arcā,with one's whole cash-box staked,: eburnis quadrigis cotidie in abaco,: apud quem alea lusum esse dicetur,: senatus consultum vetuit in pecuniam ludere,to play for money,: ego nisi quom lusim nil morer ullum lucrum,. —
With acc.: aleam,; ; : par impar,; : ducatus et imperia,: Trojam,; : proelia latronum,; cf. pass.: sunt aliis scriptae, quibus alea luditur, artes,: alea luditur,: aleae ludendae causa,: alea ludebatur,.—
Absol.: lusimus per omnes dies,; ; cf.: ludis circensibus elephantos lusisse,appeared in the public games,.—In sup.: dimittere lusum,.—
To play, sport, frisk, frolic: dum se exornat, nos volo Ludere inter nos,have some fun,: ludere armis,: suppeditant et campus noster et studia venandi honesta exempla ludendi,: ad ludendumne, an ad pugnandum, arma sumturi,: in numerum,dance,: hic juvenum series teneris immixta puellis ludit,: cumque marinae In sicco ludunt fulicae,: in exiguo cymba lacu,. —
Trop.
To sport, play with any thing, to practise as a pastime, amuse one's self with any thing: illa ipsa ludens conjeci in communes locos, prooem.: Prima Syracosio dignata est ludere versu Nostra ... Thalia,.—Esp., to play on an instrument of music, to make or compose music or song: ludere quae vellem calamo permisit agresti,: talia fumosi luduntur mense Decembri,: quod tenerae cantent, lusit tua musa, puellae,: coloni Versibus incomptis ludunt,: carmina pastorum,; : si quid vacui sub umbra Lusimus tecum,.—
To sport, dally, wanton (cf. "amorous play," Milton, P. L. 9, 1045): scis solere illam aetatem tali ludo ludere,: affatim edi, bibi, lusi, Liv. Andron. ap. Paul. ex Fest. s. v. affatim, p. 11 Müll.; cf.: lusisti satis, edisti satis, atque bibisti,; ; ; ; .—
Ludere aliquem or aliquid, to play, mock, imitate, mimic a person or thing (only in mockery; cf.: partes agere, etc.): civem bonum ludit, Cael. ap. ; cf.: ludere opus,to imitate work, make believe work,: magistratum fascibus purpurāque,: ludere causas,: impia dum Phoebi Caesar mendacia ludit, Poët. ap. .—
To trifle with: summa pericula,: viribus imperii,.—
To spend in play or amusement, to sport away: otium,.—Hence, ludere operam, to throw away one's labor, to labor in vain, .—
To make sport or game of a person, to ridicule, rally, banter: Domitius in senatu lusit Appium collegam, a, 13: satis jocose aliquem ludere,: omnium irrisione ludi,.—Rarely with ad: caput aselli, ad quod lascivi ludebant ruris alumni,.—
To delude, deceive: auditis, an me ludit amabilis Insania?; : custodes,; .—Comp.: hoc civili bello, quam multa (haruspicum responsa) luserunt,i. e. gave wanton, deceptive responses,.

la:noun:luctus.html:
luctus, ūs (
gen. lucti, Att. ap. and 32), m.
lugeo
, sorrow, mourning, grief, affliction, distress, lamentation, esp. over the loss of something dear to one.
Lit.: filius luctu perditus,: orat, ne suum luctum patris lacrimis augeatis,: in sordibus, lamentis, luctuque jacuisti,: afflictus et confectus luctu,: re cognitā tantus luctus excepit, ut, etc.,: luctu atque caede omnia complentur,: furere luctu filii,: in maximos luctus incidere,: luctum alicui importare,: dare animum in luctus,: luctus aliquando ridicula fuerit imitatio,: multis in luctibus, inque perpetuo maerore senescere,.—
Transf.
The external signs of sorrow in one's dress and gestures, mourning, mourning apparel, weeds (usually worn by the bereaved, and also by accused persons): erat in luctu senatus, squalebat civitas, publico consilio mutatā veste,: omnia discessu meo plena luctūs et maeroris fuerunt,: senatusconsulto diebus triginta luctus est finitus,: Plancina luctum amissae sororis tum primum laeto cultu mutavit,: minuitur populo luctus aedis dedicatione ... privatis autem, cum liberi nati sunt, etc.,

Fest. s. v. minuitur, p. 154 Müll.—

A source of grief: tu non inventa repertā Luctus eras levior,; cf.: et luctum et curam effugies,.—
Personified: Luctus, the god of grief: primisque in faucibus Orci Luctus et ultrices posuere cubilia Curae,; ; .

la:verb:lugeo.html:
lūgĕo, xi, ctum, 2 (luxti for luxisti, ;
dep. lugeri, ), v. n. and a. [akin to Gr. λυγρός, λοιγός; Sanscr. root lū, to cut; cf. lues], to mourn, lament, bewail, deplore (syn. ploro).
Lit.
Neutr.: luget senatus, maeret equester ordo,: annum feminis ad lugendum constituere majores,; : hos pro me lugere,.—Impers. pass.: sei ad pii rogum fili lugetur. etc.,.—
Act.: lugere mortem Trebonii, Cic. Phil. 12, 10, 25: quid ego nunc lugeam vitam hominum?: occasum atque interitum rei publicae,: ut ager lugere dominum videretur,: matronae annum, ut parentem, eum luxerunt,.—In pass.: lugebere nobis, Lugebisque alios,: parentes et filii majores X annis anno lugendi sunt,: servus matronis lugendus,.—With acc. and inf.: urbem e suis faucibus ereptam esse,: in dominos vanas luget abisse minas, Claud. ap. prooem.—
With gen.: lugere formae,.—
Transf., to be in mourning, to wear mourning apparel (v. luctus): nec lugentibus id facere fas est,: qui luget, abstinere debet a conviviis, ornamentis et albā veste,: pullo lugentes vellere lanas,fit for mourning,.

la:verb:luceo.gloss: to be light, clear; to shine, glitter
senses: to be light, clear; to shine, glitter
la:verb:luceo.html:
lūcĕo, xi, 2, v. n.
Sanscr. ruk, to be bright; Gr. λύχνος, λευκός, ἀμφιλύκη; Lat. lux, lumen, lucidus, luna; O. H.-Germ. liŏht; Germ. Licht; cf. also illustris
,
to be light or clear, to shine, beam, glitter (syn.: splendeo, fulgeo).
Lit.: (lumen) Nihilo minus ipsi lucet, Enn. ap. (Trag. v. 389 Vahl.): tum candida lumina lucent, id. ap. and 229 Müll. (Ann. v. 157 Vahl.): (stella) luce lucebat aliena,: dum meus assiduo luceat igne focus,: lucet igne rogus,: rara per occultos lucebat semita calles,: lucet via longo Ordine flammarum,; cf. (3, 6), 17: interior caeli qua semita lucet,: (luminaria) lucent in firmamento caeli,: niveo lucet in ore rubor,: lucent oculi,; : cinis in multam noctem pertinaciter luxit,: virgatis lucent sagulis (sc. Galli),glitter,: taedā lucebis in illa,i. e. shall burn,: non amplius erit sol ad lucendum,.—In the part. pres.: e rosea sol alte lampade lucens,; so, globus lunae,: faces,: sedebat In solio Phoebus claris lucente smaragdis,: lucerna lucens in caliginoso loco, Pet. 1, 19.—Poet., with acc.: huic lucebis novae nuptae facem,will light her home with a torch,: tute tibi puer es; lautus luces cereum,.—
Of the day, daylight, etc., to appear, dawn, become light: an umquam lucebit in orbe ille dies,: lucente jam die,.—
Esp., impers.: lucet, lucebat, etc., it is (was) light, it is (was) day, it is dawning: priusquam lucet, adsunt,: si lucet lucet: lucet autem, lucet igitur,: si judicatum erit meridie non lucere,: nondum lucebat,: nec satis lucebat: cum autem luceret, etc.,, a, 1: ubi lucere coepisset,: expergiscere: lucet hoc, it is light, it is day there (in the sky), : hoc ... luce lucebit,. —
Transf., to shine or show through, to be discernible, visible (poet.): si qua Arabio lucet bombyce puella, (2, 3, 15): femineum lucet sic per bombycina corpus,: vitalia lucent,are uncovered,.—
Trop., to shine forth, to be conspicuous, apparent, clear, evident: nunc imperii nostri splendor illis gentibus lucet,: mea officia et studia, quae parum antea luxerunt,: cum res ipsa tot, tam claris argumentis luceat,: virtus lucet in tenebris,: tota oratio lucet,; .—Hence, lūcens, entis, P. a., shining, bright, conspicuous: lucentior usus, Mall. Theod. de Metr. 9, 7.

la:verb:lucesco.html:
lūcesco and lūcisco, ĕre,
v. inch. n. [luceo], to begin to shine.
Lit.
In gen.: sol lucescit,: quorum caput flavo capillorum crine lucescat, Firm. Math. 4, 13.—
In partic., of the break of day, to grow light, break, dawn: nonae lucescunt,.—
Impers.: lucescit or luciscit, the day is breaking: eamus, Amphitruo: luciscit hoc jam, it is getting light there (in the sky), ; ; v. luceo, I. A. fin.: cum

lucisceret, as soon as it grew light, at break of day, *: et jam lucescebat,.—

Trop.: luciscens amor,bright, Mai.

senses: of or pertaining to a bequest or gift; bequeathed or given
la:adj:lucrativus.html:
lū^crātīvus, a, um, adj.
id.
,
gaining, attended with gain.
In gen., gainful, profitable, lucrative (rare but class.): apricatio in illo lucrativo sole, B. and K.: opera,; Spald. N. cr.: lucrativa in tantis negotiis tempora, Mai.: potu,.—
In partic., in jurid. Lat.: res lucrativae, things bequeathed or given to a person (because the acquisition is pure gain, without payment), ; : ex causa lucrativa habere (acquirere) aliquid, to receive something by bequest or as a gift, pr.; 40, 1, 4: ex causa lucrativa (fundus) meus factus est,; so, lucrativa possessio,; : lucrativa usucapio,: lucrativa acquisitio,.

la:noun:lux.html:
lux, lūcis (adverb. abl. luce, luci, and lucu, and in these old forms also used as m.;
v.infra; in Plaut. lux is usually m.; Brix ad ), f.
luceo
, light.
Lit.
In gen., the light of the sun and other heavenly bodies: cum id solis luce videatur clarius,; ; ; : per umbras Stella facem ducens multā cum luce cucurrit,: a lucifero donec lux occidat, till sunset, Juv, 13, 158. —The light, splendor, brightness of shining bodies: viridi cum luce zmaragdi,: luce coruscus ahenā,: lucem non fundentes gemmae,: ferri,.—
In partic., the light of day, daylight, day: diurna,: Metellus cum primā luce in campum currebat,: ante lucem,: primā luce ad eum accurrit,at daybreak, dawn of day,: luce sub ipsā,on the very verge of day,: in luci,by day,: luce reversā,.—Hence,
In abl. adverb.: luce, luci, and (ante-class.) lucu, by daylight, in the daytime: ut luce palam in foro saltet,; so, luce,; ; : nocte ac luce,: ut veniamus luci,: cum luci simul,: luci claro,; cf. : quis audeat luci,: quodsi luce quoque canes latrent,; : cum primo lucu ibo hinc,: cum primo luci,.—
Transf.
The heavenly bodies: illae, quae fulgent luces,.—
A day: centesima lux est ab interitu P. Clodii,: longiore luce ad id certamen nobis opus est,: anxia nocte, anxia luce gemit,: crastina,: natali die mihi dulcior haec lux,: septima quaeque lux,; cf.: natura volvente vices et lucis et anni,. —Hence, poet.: lux aestiva,summer,: lux brumalis,winter,.—
Life: qui ab Orco mortuom me reducem in lucem feceris,: corpora luce carentum,i. e. of the dead,; ; cf.: simul atque editi in lucem sumus,.—
An eye, the eyesight: effossae squalent vestigia lucis,: damnum lucis ademptae,.—
A light, of an eminent man to whom all eyes turn: Luce nihil gestum, nihil est Diomede remoto,.—Of a beloved person: o lux salve candida,.—
Trop.
The sight of all men, the public view, the public, the world: nec vero ille in luce modo, atque in oculis civium magnus sed intus domique praestantior,: Isocrates forensi luce caruit, : familiam abjectam et obscu ram e tenebris in lucem vocare,: res occultas aperire in lucemque proferre,.—
Light, encouragement, help, succor: lux quaedam videbatur oblata, non modo regno, sed etiam regni timore sublato,: civibus lucem ingenii et consilii porrigere,; cf.: lucem adferre rei publicae,.—
A light, an ornament: hanc urbem, lucem orbis terrarum,: genus sine luce,undistinguished, obscure,.—
Light, illustration, elucidation: historia testis temporum, lux veritatis,.—
That which enlightens, the source of illumination: ratio quasi quaedam lux lumenque vitae. ; cf.: ego sum lux mundi,; .

la:noun:Lupercus.html:
Lŭpercus, i, m.
lupus, and perh. arceo

The Roman name of the Lycean Pan (so called because he protected the flocks from wolves), .—Far more freq.,
A priest of the Lycean Pan: nudi Luperci,; : nec prodest agili palmas praebere Luperco,. There were at first two classes of these priests, the Fabiani and the Quintiliani, to whom afterwards, in honor of Cæsar, were added the Juliani, . At first the priests were chosen only from the herdsmen, but afterwards young persons of the highest rank were received among them: ita eras Lupercus, ut te consulem esse meminisse deberes,; .— There were also Luperci at Velitrae,.

Lit.: torva leaena lupum sequitur, lupus ipse capellam,; ; : Martialis lupus,sacred to Mars,; so, Martius,: lupus femina for lupa, a she-wolf, Enn. ap. (Ann. v. 70 Vahl.); id. ap. (): lupus masculinum (est), quamquam Varro ... lupum feminam dicit, Ennium Pictoremque Fabium secutus,.—According to the belief of the Romans, if a wolf saw a man before the latter saw him, the man became dumb: vox quoque Moerim Jam fugit ipsa; lupi Moerim videre priores,; cf. .—Prov.: lupus in fabulā or sermone, said of the appearance of a person when he is spoken of; as we say in English, talk of the devil, and he appears: atque eccum tibi lupum in sermone,; ; : de Varrone loquebamur: lupus in fabulā: venit enim ad me,.—
